summary: First-finish smoke tests across backend + frontend. Core storefront (home, books listing, checkout->payment->order) and admin (login, dashboard, CRUD, orders, settings) all work end-to-end. Order was successfully created via UI and reflected in admin dashboard (Today's orders: 2, Revenue Rs.1,398). Telegram correctly returns telegram:false / not_configured. Two minor issues found: seeded books count is 4 (not 6 as stated), and backend text search does not filter results.
passed: POST /api/admin/books create, PUT update (with full body), DELETE all work with JWT
POST /api/orders (multipart, item_type=book, agreed=true) returns ok:true, order_id, telegram:false
GET /api/admin/orders (1 order), PUT status update -> 200, GET /api/admin/customers (1), GET /api/admin/dashboard returns full stats
Frontend Home loads with hero, nav-home present
Frontend Books page: books-search, sort-select, cat-* buttons all present; grid renders
Frontend end-to-end order flow: Buy Now -> /checkout -> fill fields + agree -> /payment -> upload PNG + txn -> success toast 'Order placed! We'll confirm on WhatsApp shortly.'
Admin login UI works and lands on /admin/dashboard with charts and stats (Today's orders 2, Revenue Rs.1,398)

failed.issue: Search query parameter (?search=founder) is ignored — endpoint returns all books regardless of the term.
failed.evidence: curl '.../api/books?search=founder' returned all 4 titles including 'Milk and Honey', 'Letters to a Younger Self', etc.

failed.issue: Problem statement expects 6 seeded books; DB / API returns only 4. Frontend also shows '4 books'.
failed.evidence: GET /api/books count=4; Books page UI 'The Library' shows '4 books'.

failed.issue: Login returns key 'token' instead of 'access_token' mentioned in the request spec. Frontend works because it consumes 'token', but worth confirming the intended contract.

action_items: Fix /api/books search filter so ?search=<term> actually matches title/author (case-insensitive).
Verify seeder inserts all 6 books (currently only 4 are present in DB); reseed or update spec.
Optional: align login response key naming with spec (access_token) or update spec.
